theme: End-of-season tomato sugo + brothy white beans — two Saturday batches that carry a full-house week of rustic Italian dinners the girls will actually eat.

components.name: End-of-Season Tomato Sugo
components.ingredients: 5 lb ripe tomatoes (or 2x 28oz San Marzano if the fresh ones are past it), 1 large onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery rib, 4 garlic cloves, generous olive oil, basil stems, pinch chili, salt
components.method: Build a slow soffritto: finely dice onion, carrot and celery and sweat gently in a good pour of olive oil over low heat 12-15 min until soft and sweet, not browned. Add sliced garlic for a minute, then the tomatoes (crush fresh by hand, or the canned ones), a few basil stems, salt and a pinch of chili. Simmer uncovered on low 45-60 min, stirring now and then, until glossy and thick. Fish out the basil stems. Cool and store ~3 qt in jars; keeps 5 days in the fridge, freezes well.

components.name: Brothy White Bean Conserva
components.ingredients: 1 lb dried cannellini or gigante beans (soaked overnight), 1 onion halved, 1 head garlic halved crosswise, 4 sage leaves, 2 bay, a wide strip of lemon peel, olive oil, salt
components.method: Drain the soaked beans into a pot, cover by two inches with fresh water, add onion, garlic, sage, bay, lemon peel and a big glug of olive oil. Bring to a bare simmer and hold it there — never a hard boil, which splits the skins — for 60-90 min until completely creamy. Salt generously only in the last 15 min. Cool the beans IN their liquid; that starchy, olive-oiled broth is half the point. Store ~6 cups beans plus liquid; keeps 5 days.

dinners.name: Rigatoni al Pomodoro
dinners.ingredients: 1.5 lb rigatoni, ~1 qt tomato sugo, parmesan, basil, olive oil, splash pasta water
steps: Boil rigatoni in well-salted water until just shy of al dente.
Warm the sugo in a wide pan with a little olive oil.
Drag the pasta straight into the sauce with a splash of pasta water; toss hard 1-2 min so it emulsifies and coats.
Off heat, fold in a handful of grated parm and torn basil. Serve with extra parm at the table for the girls.

dinners.name: Seared Cod over White Beans
dinners.ingredients: 6 cod or hake fillets (~2 lb), the white beans + their broth, a bunch of spinach or chard, lemon, garlic, olive oil
steps: Warm the beans with a ladle of their broth and a clove of smashed garlic; wilt in the greens, keep loose and brothy. Spoon into shallow bowls.
Pat cod very dry, salt it. Heat olive oil in a nonstick or well-seasoned pan until shimmering.
Lay fillets in presentation-side down; don't move them 3-4 min until a golden crust releases cleanly.
Flip, cut the heat, and spoon the hot oil over the top (arroser) 1 min to finish. Set fish on the beans, finish with lemon and oil. Flake the girls' portions off the bone-free fillet.

dinners.name: Chicken Cacciatora over Soft Polenta
dinners.ingredients: 8 bone-in chicken thighs, ~1 qt tomato sugo, 1 sliced bell pepper, splash white wine, rosemary, 1.5 cups polenta, butter/parm
steps: Brown salted thighs skin-side down in olive oil until deeply golden; remove.
Soften the pepper in the fat, deglaze with wine, add the sugo and a rosemary sprig.
Nestle the thighs back in, cover partway and simmer gently 25-30 min until tender.
Meanwhile cook polenta soft and loose, finish with butter and parm. Spoon chicken and sauce over; kids get pulled chicken on polenta.

dinners.name: Pasta e Fagioli
dinners.ingredients: the white beans + broth, ~1 cup tomato sugo, 1 cup small pasta (ditalini), escarole or kale, parm rind, olive oil, crusty bread
steps: Warm the beans and their broth with the sugo, a parm rind and enough water to make it soupy.
Add a couple handfuls of chopped escarole or kale; simmer 8 min.
Stir in ditalini and cook right in the pot until tender, adding water as it drinks it up.
Mash a ladle of beans against the side for body. Big glug of raw olive oil per bowl, parm and bread alongside.

technique.name: Pan-searing delicate fish + arroser (oil basting)
technique.tiedTo: The seared cod over white beans — dry the fillet hard, get the oil truly shimmering, and leave it undisturbed until the crust releases on its own; then cut the heat and spoon the hot oil over to finish gently instead of overcooking the second side. Nails the crisp-outside, just-set-inside fish that makes simple seafood feel restaurant-level.

shopping.items: 5 lb ripe tomatoes, 2 onions, 1 carrot, 1 celery rib, 2 heads garlic, 1 bell pepper, spinach or chard, escarole or kale, 2 lemons, basil, rosemary, sage, bay
6 cod or hake fillets (~2 lb), skinless and boneless
parmesan (a good wedge, keep the rind), butter
1 lb dried cannellini or gigante beans, 1.5 lb rigatoni, 1 cup ditalini, 1.5 cups polenta, 2x 28oz San Marzano tomatoes (backup), good olive oil, dried chili, white wine, salt

scaleNote: This week is a FULL HOUSE (2 adults + 4 girls under 10), so the quantities above already feed 6 with mild, kid-friendly plates: sugo and beans are batched big (~3 qt sugo, ~6 cups beans) to cover all four dinners with a little to spare. For the girls, keep heat low (chili on the side), serve fish flaked and chicken pulled off the bone, and let them build their own bowls with extra parm. On the alternating 2-adult weeks, halve the pasta, fish and chicken but still make the full component batches — they freeze, and give you a head start on the quiet week's more technique-forward cooking.
